blocks.content: The Central Information Commission is a vital instrument for promoting transparency, accountability, and citizen empowerment in the functioning of public authorities.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Information Commission (CIC) is an independent statutory body constituted under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
It acts as the highest appellate authority for RTI applications related to Central Government departments and Union Territories.
The Commission promotes transparency, accountability, and good governance by curbing corruption and empowering citizens.
CIC has the powers of a civil court while inquiring into any matter under the RTI Act, including summoning persons and inspecting public records.
The members are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and a nominated Union Cabinet Minister.
CIC is a Statutory body, NOT a Constitutional body; it was created by an Act of Parliament (RTI Act, 2005).
Selection Committee Composition: Prime Minister (Chairperson), Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.
Reappointment Rule: The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners are NOT eligible for reappointment.
RTI Amendment Act 2019: The term of office and conditions of service for Commissioners are now specified by the Central Government rather than fixed by statute.
